title: Deep-learning-assisted DIP-MS identifies POLR2E as a constitutive prefoldin-like-complex subunit
summary: DIP-MS combines deep-learning-based signal processing with native-gel fractionation and mass spectrometry to resolve complex isoforms. In human prefoldin-like-complex experiments, repeated coelution and affinity-purification data supported POLR2E as a constitutive PFDL component, updating the view that it was merely an associated protein.
ai_technology: Deep Interactome Profiling by Mass Spectrometry (DIP-MS), including deep-learning-based signal processing
organization: Institute of Molecular Systems Biology, ETH Zurich and collaborators

evidence.tested: In human prefoldin-like-complex experiments, repeated coelution and affinity-purification data supported POLR2E as a constitutive PFDL component, updating the view that it was merely an associated protein.
evidence.unknown: The paper proposes POLR2E as a constitutive PFDL subunit based on coelution and affinity-purification in the tested human-cell system; it does not establish that every cellular PFDL complex contains POLR2E or fully characterize its functional contribution. DIP-MS also recapitulated known ASDURF association, which is not counted here as novel because ASDURF’s PAQosome/PFDL role had been reported earlier.
evidence.ai_role: Deep-learning signal processing helped resolve coexisting protein-complex isoforms from AP-MS/native PAGE/DIA-MS data. DIP-MS on UXT and PFDN2 baits repeatedly detected PFDL coelution with POLR2E; affinity purification of four tagged PFDL-like subunits also recovered POLR2E, supporting the proposed constitutive association.
